blindWork: Heat lost by hot water = 50.0 x 4.184 x (60.0 - 38.5) = 50.0 x 4.184 x 21.5 = 4498 J. Heat gained by cold water = 50.0 x 4.184 x (38.5 - 20.0) = 3870 J. Difference = 628 J absorbed by the cup, so C_cal = 628/18.5 = 33.9 J/degC.
stem: Coffee-Cup Calorimeter Heat Capacity: To measure the heat capacity of a polystyrene coffee-cup calorimeter, $50.0\text{~mL}$ of hot water at ${60.0}^{\circ}\text{C}$ is added to $50.0\text{~mL}$ of cold water at ${20.0}^{\circ}\text{C}$ inside the cup. The final equilibrium temperature is ${38.5}^{\circ}\text{C}$. Taking the specific heat of water as $4.184\text{~J/(g} \cdot^{\circ}\text{C)}$ and density as $1.00\text{~g/mL}$, what is the heat capacity of the calorimeter ($C_{cal}$)?
sourceExplanation: Heat lost by hot water $= 50.0 \times 4.184 \times (60.0 - 38.5) = 4497.8\text{~J}$. Heat gained by cold water $= 50.0 \times 4.184 \times (38.5 - 20.0) = 3870.2\text{~J}$. Heat gained by calorimeter $= 4497.8 - 3870.2 = 627.6\text{~J}$. $C_{cal} = 627.6/(38.5 - 20.0) = 33.9\text{~J/}^{\circ}\text{C}$. (Correct option: B)
